label: wherewhen - Analysis Engine
info:
Fulgrim Flux analysis engine (PLAN.md §11) — computes all 20 planned analyses and pushes each result to GoDaddy's api/analysis_push.php, where analysis.php already has real page shells reading analysis_results (built earlier, independent of this flow, per CLAUDE.md's GoDaddy-first build order).

DESIGN CALLS made building this (PLAN.md left both open):
1. Flux itself only ever does from|range|filter|sort — the same primitives already proven working elsewhere in this project (wherewhen_data_export/restore's queries). ALL statistics (Pearson correlation, linear trend slope, clustering counts) are computed in plain JS after the CSV comes back, not inside Flux's own covariance/stats packages, since those have never been confirmed against this project's actual InfluxDB install. Matches PLAN.md's own framing: "Node-RED orchestrates... shapes results."
2. Every analysis runs at every tier that fires (daily/weekly/monthly/all), just over that tier's own window, rather than hand-assigning which analyses belong to which tier. Simpler one-path design; the cost is some redundant recompute, cheap at this project's actual data volume.
3. Tier windows (not specified by PLAN.md): daily=trailing 90 days, weekly=trailing 180 days, monthly=trailing 400 days, all=since 2025-08-01 (a safe early anchor, not precisely researched). Daily/weekly/monthly are scheduled; all-data is manual-only (same reasoning as oura_backfill_flow.json being manual — the heaviest, least time-sensitive tier).

The analysis registry (ANALYSES, ~20 entries) is duplicated verbatim into both 'Build Flux query for this analysis' and 'Parse response + shape result' — both need it (query-building happens before the InfluxDB HTTP call, shaping happens after the response returns, and Node-RED function nodes don't share JS scope across nodes), matching this project's existing preference for self-contained nodes over a shared-context module pattern this project has never used elsewhere.

keys in ANALYSES MUST stay in sync with godaddy/app/analysis.php's own $analyses list — confirmed matching 1:1 at build time (all 20 keys, both directions), but nothing enforces that automatically if either side changes later.

UNTESTED, same as everything else in this project's HA side — built from documented Flux/InfluxDB CSV behavior and this repo's own already-proven query/parse patterns, never run against Ward's real InfluxDB. Field/measurement names themselves ARE ground-truth — read directly from the actual line-protocol-building code in oura_sync_flow.json/godaddy_pull_flow.json/body_comp_import_flow.json, not guessed from PLAN.md's prose descriptions.

Watches /share/lucius_body_comp_import/ for .xlsx exports from Ward's smart scale, parses every file with node-red-contrib-officedocs (API confirmed working via body_comp_xlsx_test.json — see that flow's tab info for how the exceljs 'read'/'readRange' operations were verified), collapses to one reading per calendar day (keeping the latest), writes all 13 rich metrics to InfluxDB's body_composition measurement, pushes just that day's weight to GoDaddy's api/weight_push.php (which only ever sets daily_logs.weight if it's currently NULL — never overwrites), then moves processed files into processed/.

Column order (A–Q, 17 columns) is taken directly from the confirmed table in PLAN.md §14, matched against the same 'A1:Q41' range already proven correct in the test flow.

label: Lucius - GoDaddy API Test
info:
Manual companion test for every WardStock Node-RED flow that calls GoDaddy api/*.php (PLAN.md §2 standing rule). Click the inject node to run. Does NOT run on a schedule.

1. Reads /share/lucius_secrets.json (same path production flows use — /share, not the Node-RED add-on's own /config).
2. Debugs: file found, parse OK, key names (not secret values), resolved godaddy_base_url, and every constructed API URL + method. Bearer tokens are redacted to length + last 4.
3. Live HTTP with the same Authorization: Bearer godaddy_api_sync_token the production flows send:
   - GET api/status.php — expect 200
   - GET api/get_shared_config.php — expect 200 (oura_client_id/secret redacted in debug)
   - POST empty JSON {} to oura_push / status_push / weight_push / incident_push / analysis_push — expect 400 malformed_request. That proves the endpoint exists and accepted the token WITHOUT writing a row. Do not send a valid oura/weight/incident/analysis payload from this flow — there is no dry-run flag on those PHP files.
   - GET api/pull_manual_data.php is constructed and printed but NOT called: that script always updates last_ha_pull_at, which would move the production 15-min pull bookmark.

Expected live base URL: https://aileeward.com/wardstock (lowercase path). The parse step flags emperorschildren.net or /Wardstock if they are still in the secrets file.

UNTESTED against a live stack until you run it — same caveat as system_test_flow.json. See homeassistant/README.md for import (Menu → Import; watch for a duplicate tab on re-import).

label: Lucius - GoDaddy Backup
info:
Runs once a day (3am) plus a manual trigger. Pulls the FULL current state of incidents/Daily Log/Therapy/Medications/dosage-history from GoDaddy (api/pull_manual_data.php?scope=all — deliberately the full set every run, not since-last, so this is a true daily mirror rather than an accumulating log) and:

1. Writes every record as one row of raw JSON into a dedicated local SQLite database, /share/lucius_godaddy_backup.db (table godaddy_backup) — a full REPLACE each run (old rows for a type are cleared before the fresh set is written), so a record deleted on GoDaddy doesn't linger forever as 'restorable' here. This is the real disaster-recovery copy: Ward's own framing, Aug 2026, 'we are wiping the godaddy database... GoDaddy is the source of truth for entered data, so read from GoDaddy, then keep HA's copy in sync, in case we need to restore it.'
2. Also writes the same structured numeric fields to InfluxDB as time series (same line-building logic godaddy_pull_flow.json already uses for its own 15-minute pull) — this is for wherewhen's own correlation queries, not disaster recovery; duplicate points across the two flows are harmless (InfluxDB merges same-timestamp/same-tag writes).

Deliberately NOT limited to a 60-day window, unlike an earlier draft of this feature — the whole point is recovering from a wiped GoDaddy database, which needs full history, not just a recent slice. EKG recordings are out of scope for this flow (Ward's own list: therapy sessions, medicine changes, weights, incidents, caffeine/alcohol — all covered by the 5 record types above; EKG has no restore-side push endpoint yet either).

Pairs with godaddy_restore_flow.json (manual-only) — that flow reads this same SQLite table back out and POSTs it to the new api/bulk_restore.php endpoint to actually repopulate a wiped GoDaddy database.

UNTESTED — built from godaddy_pull_flow.json's proven-live patterns (same secrets read, same InfluxDB line-building, same job-status SQLite table) but never run end-to-end itself. Verify the schedule trigger, http request, and sqlite node configs against your actual Node-RED version after import.

label: GoDaddy Backup - Test & Validate
info:
Companion test flow for godaddy_backup_flow.json (PLAN.md §2's standing rule: every live flow gets one — this one was originally missing, flagged as a gap, now built). Exercises the SQLite-serialization half of that flow in isolation, against a hand-built fixture standing in for a pull_manual_data.php response, using the SAME row-building code (record_type filter + SQL string-escaping + JSON.stringify) duplicated verbatim from n_gb_process — not a reimplementation that could quietly drift from what the real flow actually runs.

What it checks, against a throwaway scratch table (godaddy_backup_test) in the same scratch DB file sqlite_test_flow.json already uses (/share/lucius_sqlite_test.db) — never touches the real /share/lucius_godaddy_backup.db:
1. Round-trip fidelity: five in-scope record types (incident, daily_log, therapy_session, medication, medication_dosage_history), each carrying deliberately awkward content — embedded single quotes, double quotes, a literal SQL-comment sequence, a newline, and non-ASCII text — survive CREATE→escape→INSERT OR REPLACE→SELECT→JSON.parse exactly unchanged.
2. Scope filtering: an ecg_recording fixture and a made-up future record_type are correctly EXCLUDED from what gets written — confirms the real flow's inScope allowlist actually works, not just that it exists in the code.
3. Natural-key behavior: two fixture rows sharing the same (record_type, source_id) — simulating a re-run backing up the same GoDaddy id twice — collapse to one row (INSERT OR REPLACE), not two.

Does NOT exercise the HTTP/secrets/InfluxDB half of the real flow — that logic is identical to godaddy_pull_flow.json's own already-relied-upon pattern, not new here. Also does not call the real GoDaddy API or write real InfluxDB points, by design — this is offline/isolated, same as every other companion test flow in this project.

UNTESTED like every other flow in this project — the SQLite CREATE/INSERT/SELECT/DROP sequence and node-red-node-sqlite's query/result shape ARE separately confirmed against Ward's real instance (sqlite_test_flow.json Part A), so this flow's own mechanics carry high confidence; what's specifically unverified is this flow itself, end to end, on a real deploy.

Does NOT touch EKG recordings (out of scope for the backup half too) or anything InfluxDB-only (Oura raw archive, body composition, analysis results — those are wherewhen_data_restore_flow.json's job, a separate flow, separate direction of 'source of truth').

No separate companion test flow, same reasoning as oura_backfill_flow.json — this manual, on-demand flow already functions as its own diagnostic tool; the debug sidebar shows exactly what got read from SQLite and what api/bulk_restore.php reported back.

label: Lucius - GoDaddy Restore (from file)
info:
Manual trigger ONLY, same 'wipe/migrate scenario, not routine' convention as godaddy_restore_flow.json and wherewhen_data_restore_flow.json. Sibling to godaddy_restore_flow.json (which restores from HA's own local SQLite mirror) — this one instead restores from an arbitrary external WardStock-export-shaped JSON file, for exactly the situation Ward hit Aug 2026: a mysqldump/phpMyAdmin SQL backup existed but HA's own SQLite mirror didn't have anything backed up yet (godaddy_backup_flow.json never having run against that data), so there was no flow that could import that backup at all.

Expects /share/lucius_restore_import.json to already exist on the HA box, in the exact shape api/pull_manual_data.php / export.php already produce: {"records": [...]}, each record tagged with record_type (incident / daily_log / therapy_session / medication / medication_dosage_history). A raw .sql dump is NOT a supported input directly — no SQL parser lives in Node-RED here, on purpose (this project's own convention: don't build a general-purpose thing when a narrow one solves the actual problem). Converting a mysqldump into this shape is a one-off task performed once, outside Node-RED (Claude did this for the Aug 2026 restore — see ForWard/wardstock_restore_from_sql_backup.json and its own generation notes); this flow is the reusable, permanent half — it will import ANY file in the correct shape, not just that one conversion.

Copy the converted JSON to /share/lucius_restore_import.json (via Studio Code Server or the Samba/SFTP share, same as any other /share file this project already uses) before running.

POSTs straight through to the same api/bulk_restore.php as godaddy_restore_flow.json — same import_records() merge-safe logic, same 'nothing was saved on any failure partway through' transaction guarantee. Does NOT write to HA's local godaddy_backup SQLite table itself — after a successful run, GoDaddy has the data; run godaddy_backup_flow.json afterward (or wait for its 3am schedule) to bring HA's own local mirror back in sync with what's now on GoDaddy, same as any other time GoDaddy's data changes.

No companion test flow — reuses api/bulk_restore.php and the merge-safe logic already exercised by godaddy_backup_test.json's fixture-round-trip checks and (once run for real) godaddy_restore_flow.json itself; the only genuinely new logic here is the file-read + shape-validation step, small enough that this flow's own tab info and debug output serve the same purpose a dedicated test flow would.

UNTESTED — same caveat as every new flow in this project. Read the whole tab info before running against a real GoDaddy database.

label: Lucius - Medical History Import
info:
Manual/on-demand — not scheduled (PLAN.md §19). Watches /share/lucius_medical_history_import/ for *.yaml files matching the structured medical-history import format documented in PLAN.md §19, upserts one `cardiac`/`medical`-category incident per `encounters[]` entry via the new token-authenticated api/incident_push.php (idempotent on the YAML entry's `id` slug, stored as `incidents.external_ref`), then moves processed files into processed/.

`symptom_context`/`therapy_history_reference`/`open_research_items` in the YAML are deliberately NOT read by this flow — per PLAN.md §19, those have no ingestible date (or aren't incident-shaped data at all) and stay reference-only in the file itself.

label: TEST - medical history YAML parsing
info:
Companion test flow for medical_history_import_flow.json (PLAN.md §2's standing rule — every live flow gets one, kept permanently). Exercises Node-RED's CORE `yaml` node (bundled with Node-RED itself, not a third-party package — but this is the first place any of this project's flows have used it, so still worth confirming rather than assuming) against a small embedded YAML fixture matching PLAN.md §19's documented schema, rather than depending on a real file existing at /share/lucius_medical_history_import/ on whatever HA instance this runs on — self-contained, portable, no setup required to run this test.

What this confirms: (1) the yaml node actually converts a YAML string into a JS object with the expected shape — encounters as an array, each entry's fields present and correctly typed (not stringified numbers, not missing nested fields); (2) core split on an array property behaves as expected, same mechanism the live flow relies on twice. If the yaml node's output shape ever turns out to differ from what's assumed here (e.g. it wraps output differently, or a palette update changes behavior), this is where that would show up first — re-run this after any Node-RED/palette upgrade that touches core nodes, not just after touching this project's own flows.

label: Lucius - Oura Backfill
info:
Manual, on-demand flow (not scheduled) to backfill full-fidelity historical Oura data straight into InfluxDB, bypassing GoDaddy's curated summary entirely -- a manual pull through GoDaddy only captures sleep_duration_hrs/sleep_efficiency/resting_hr/hrv/steps (a small curated subset). This flow archives everything oura_sync_flow.json's InfluxDB half already logs for live data -- every scalar field per record, plus decomposed 5-minute heart_rate/hrv time series -- for a whole historical range instead of just 'today'.

HOW TO USE: open the 'Manual trigger' inject node, edit its JSON payload to the range you want -- {"start_date":"YYYY-MM-DD","end_date":"YYYY-MM-DD"} -- then click it (the button on the node, or Deploy then click). Re-edit and re-click for a different range; nothing about this flow remembers a previous range.

ANSWERING THE 'does it know where the data is' QUESTION: no discovery step exists or is needed -- you just pick a range as wide as you want (even back before you started wearing the ring), and Oura's API simply returns whatever real records actually exist inside it; periods with nothing recorded just come back empty, not as an error. An overly wide range costs a few empty pages, nothing worse.

PAGINATION: unlike the live sync flow's narrow 3-day window (which only ever needed one page), a real historical range can span many pages of Oura's cursor-based next_token pagination. This flow loops each of the three endpoints (sleep, daily_activity, daily_readiness) in turn until next_token stops appearing, with a 500-page safety cap per endpoint (warns and stops cleanly with whatever was collected so far if that cap is ever actually hit, rather than looping forever).

WRITES TO INFLUXDB IN CHUNKS (500 lines per POST, brief pause between chunks) rather than one giant request -- a multi-year backfill with decomposed heart_rate/hrv series can produce tens of thousands of lines, and one request that size risks hitting a body-size limit somewhere in the chain for no real benefit over a few hundred smaller ones. The debug panel shows a running 'writing chunk N/M' message per chunk plus a final summary line, so a long backfill still gives visible progress.

Does NOT push anything to GoDaddy or touch HA helper entities -- this is purely a raw-data archival tool for InfluxDB. Does still log a start/finish point to InfluxDB's sync_job_runs measurement (job_name=oura_backfill), same convention as the other flows, so a run is visible/confirmable there too.

UNTESTED, same caveat as every other flow in this project -- built from oura_sync_flow.json's proven-live logic (as of Aug 2026, after its Aug 2026 fixes: the missing InfluxDB start-point prep node, the NaN-unsafe token-expiry check, and the api-call-service schema change) but never run end-to-end itself yet. No separate companion test flow for this one specifically -- it's already a manual, on-demand diagnostic tool in its own right, same reasoning as why system_test_flow.json doesn't have one either (PLAN.md §2).

label: Lucius - Oura Sync
info:
Runs every 4 hours, anchored to 10am (10,14,18,22,2,6). Fetches oura_client_id/oura_client_secret fresh from GoDaddy's api/get_shared_config.php each run (PLAN.md §3 — GoDaddy is the source of truth for these, no longer hand-copied locally), pulls high-fidelity Oura data into InfluxDB, pushes summary fields to GoDaddy (one per day actually present in the fetch window, not just today — see self-heal note below), logs job start/finish to InfluxDB, updates HA status entities.

SELF-HEAL FIX (PLAN.md §1 TODO, Aug 2026): the fetch window's start now extends back to the last confirmed-data date (input_datetime.lucius_oura_last_data_date, new helper — add to ha_config/helpers.yaml) instead of always being a fixed 'yesterday', so a missed run or a day Oura had no data for yet gets caught up automatically on a later run rather than staying silently missing. Normal-case behavior is unchanged; this only ever extends the window further back, never narrows it. New split/join pairing (n_oura_split_summaries / n_oura_join_summaries) handles pushing one GoDaddy summary per day when a catch-up run spans more than one day — confirm this split/join behaves as expected in the editor after import, it's the first place this project's flows have used that Node-RED core pairing.

UNTESTED — built from the proven PHP logic in godaddy/app/oura.php but never run against a live Node-RED/InfluxDB/Oura stack. Verify the schedule trigger's cron expression in the editor after import (Node-RED's inject-node schedule UI has changed across versions) and test each HTTP Request node's config against your actual Node-RED version before trusting it end to end.

label: SQLite - Test & Validate
info:
Validates assumptions before any real SQLite migration gets built (Ward, Aug 2026) — same discipline this project has used for every new node type (officedocs, core yaml, the HA websocket palette): guess from documentation, build a throwaway test flow, run it against the real target, fix what's actually wrong.

TWO THINGS ASSUMED HERE, NOT CONFIRMED:
1. Node type. This flow uses node type "sqlite" backed by a "sqlitedb" config node — the shape of the official node-red-node-sqlite package. If your installed package is different, Node-RED will show these nodes as unrecognized/dashed on import and refuse to deploy — that's the signal, not a bug. Tell me the actual node type shown in Manage Palette and I'll rebuild against it.
2. Query/result shape. node-red-node-sqlite's own convention (moderate confidence, not verified against a real response): msg.topic carries the SQL text, msg.params carries bind parameters, results come back on msg.payload as an array of row objects for a SELECT. This flow logs the RAW payload at every step rather than asserting a shape, specifically because that shape is the thing being validated, not something to assume correct going in.

TWO SEPARATE PARTS, run independently via their own inject nodes:
- Part A (top): a throwaway scratch table in a brand-new file (/share/lucius_sqlite_test.db, auto-created, zero risk to anything real) — proves the node type/package works at all: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, INSERT, SELECT, DROP TABLE cleanup.
- Part B (bottom): a READ-ONLY check against what we're assuming is the same database the SQLite Web add-on already points at — the config node below now points at /share/lucius_status.db directly -- the database path question this test flow was originally built to answer is settled (that IS the real, shared status DB every flow in this project uses), so there is no placeholder left to edit before running Part B. Only runs `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'` — lists existing tables, changes nothing, so it's safe to point at the real file and just look.

Once both parts confirm real behavior, the actual status-tracking schema (job_name, last_success, last_attempt, last_attempt_ok, last_error) gets built as its own idempotent "ensure schema" flow — same CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pattern Part A already exercises here, mirroring godaddy/sql/upgrade_from_3.0.0.sql's own safe-to-rerun convention — run once by hand or at the start of every status-writing flow, not something requiring manual table creation in SQLite Web first.

- Part C (added after Part A/B first showed "unknown node type" — no SQLite Node-RED palette is installed): checks whether the `sqlite3` CLI binary is already present in the Node-RED add-on's own container via the core `exec` node, same one already proven working for file listing/moving in Body Comp Import/Medical History Import/both wherewhen flows — no new dependency needed just to run this check. If it's there, the real flows can shell out to it directly instead of needing any npm SQLite package at all, which matters here specifically because SQLite's native-binding Node-RED packages have a real history of failing to build on Alpine/musl-based containers (what the HA Node-RED add-on runs on) — sidestepping that risk entirely beats guessing at which palette might install cleanly.

label: Lucius - Status Heartbeat
info:
Runs every 15 minutes (PLAN.md §15). Deliberately a fifth, dedicated flow rather than each sync flow pushing its own status inline — reads the shared job_status SQLite table every status-writing flow now maintains (Aug 2026 SQLite migration, see below), computes one consolidated snapshot, pushes it to GoDaddy's api/status_push.php (feeds status.php's HA/Node-RED/Analytics view), and writes the same snapshot to InfluxDB's system_status_snapshot measurement per Ward's explicit request to keep it there for trend-watching.

SQLite MIGRATION (Aug 2026) — this flow used to chain 28 api-current-state HA reads (4 fields × 7 flows), one per helper entity, each needing its own manually-configured Server field. Replaced with a single SELECT * FROM job_status against /share/lucius_status.db (the same file every flow's job_success/job_failed nodes write to) — no HA connection needed for this flow at all anymore. dashboard.yaml's old Lovelace card, which showed 3 of these flows' HA entities directly, is retired along with the entities themselves — status.php and this flow's own InfluxDB write are now the only places this data lives.

UNTESTED, same caveat as every flow in this project — PLUS one piece of real, deliberate scope-narrowing worth knowing about: PLAN.md §15 suggested this flow also query HA's own /api/config for HA version/uptime, to give the 'HA' category more than just a heartbeat. That's NOT implemented here — it would need either a Supervisor API token or a manually-managed long-lived access token, neither of which this project otherwise needs. Instead, the 'ha' category's only component (ha_core) uses this heartbeat's own successful execution as the signal — which is still real signal: if HA/Node-RED goes down, this flow stops running, ha_core goes overdue on status.php, and that overdue state IS the answer to 'is HA up.' Richer HA-native detail is a clearly flagged open follow-up, not a silent gap.

label: wherewhen - Data Export
info:
PLAN.md §20 — backs up everything InfluxDB holds, so a wiped/migrated HA install isn't a total loss. Manual trigger, plus a weekly schedule (Sunday 3am) so a usable backup exists even if Ward forgets to run one by hand — the whole value of a backup depends on how stale it is when actually needed.

Enumerates InfluxDB measurements DYNAMICALLY via Flux's `schema.measurements()` — not a hardcoded list — so newly-added measurements (this project's data model has been growing quickly) get picked up automatically without this flow needing an edit every time. For each measurement, runs a full-range Flux query and writes InfluxDB's own CSV response body directly to /share/lucius_data_backup/<timestamp>/<measurement>.csv — no manual CSV conversion, InfluxDB's query API already returns annotated CSV natively (Content-Type: application/vnd.flux request, CSV response by default). Also writes a manifest.json (measurement list + row counts) for the Restore flow's verify mode to check against.

First place any of this project's flows queries InfluxDB (every other flow only ever writes to /api/v2/write) — genuinely new API surface, worth confirming the /api/v2/query request shape works as expected on first real run.

UNTESTED — built from InfluxDB v2's documented Flux/query API, never run against a live InfluxDB instance.

label: wherewhen - Data Restore
info:
PLAN.md §20 — reads a backup produced by wherewhen_data_export_flow.json and rewrites InfluxDB from it. Manual trigger ONLY, deliberately — explicitly for the wipe/migrate scenario (a freshly bootstrapped InfluxDB, new org/bucket/token per INFLUXDB_V2_SETUP.md), not for restoring into an instance that still has the old data. Edit the trigger's payload (backup_dir) before clicking, same pattern as oura_backfill_flow.json's manual trigger.

GoDaddy-side restore is NOT reinvented here — that stays import.php reading the existing disaster-recovery JSON archive (PLAN.md §4), which already works. This flow is strictly the InfluxDB-only half.

THE RISKIEST PART OF THIS FLOW, flagged per PLAN.md §20's own caution that this is 'the highest-stakes flow in the project': reconstructing InfluxDB line-protocol from the annotated CSV InfluxDB's query API produces (n_wdr_parse_csv_to_lines). Handles multiple table/header blocks in one CSV response (Flux groups different tag-combinations of the same measurement into separate annotated blocks) by re-detecting a new header row whenever one appears, rather than assuming exactly one header block per file — REASONED FROM DOCUMENTED FLUX CSV FORMAT, NOT CONFIRMED against a real multi-table export. Writes one field per line-protocol point rather than combining a series' multiple fields into one line — relies on InfluxDB's own documented behavior of merging same-measurement/same-tags/same-timestamp writes at the storage layer, not on this flow doing that merging itself.

Simplification, not full robustness: restores each measurement file in ONE write POST, not chunked like oura_backfill_flow.json's 500-line batches — acceptable for a rare, human-supervised operation, but flag if a real run ever hits a body-size error on a very large measurement.

Verify mode (§20's 'still open' item, resolved here): after restoring, runs a Flux count() per measurement and compares against the export manifest's row_count — a BALLPARK sanity check (the manifest's row_count includes CSV header/annotation lines, so exact equality isn't expected), not a byte-exact guarantee.

UNTESTED — never run against a live InfluxDB instance, and this flow's core logic could not be verified against real Flux CSV output during development. Companion test flow (wherewhen_data_restore_test.json) checks the CSV parser against a hand-built fixture matching the documented format, but that is not the same as a real InfluxDB response — treat this flow with real caution on first use, per its own tab info.

label: TEST - Flux CSV parser (restore)
info:
Companion test flow for wherewhen_data_restore_flow.json (PLAN.md §2's standing rule) — exercises n_wdr_parse_csv_to_lines' CSV-to-line-protocol logic in isolation against a hand-built fixture matching InfluxDB's DOCUMENTED annotated CSV format, since this logic could not be verified against a real InfluxDB response during development (flagged as the riskiest part of the whole flow in its own tab info).

This test is NOT equivalent to real verification — it confirms the parser does what it's DESIGNED to do against a fixture built from documentation, not that the documentation itself matches every real response shape InfluxDB actually produces (multiple table blocks, unusual tag combinations, etc.). Re-run this after any change to the parser logic; but treat a real backup/restore cycle against a live InfluxDB instance as the actual proof, not this test passing.
